fact: Business Tech Africa reports that fintech REasy and Africa Global Logistics are piloting a service, presented in Douala on 2026-10-01, that lets Cameroonian importers pay Chinese suppliers by converting CFA francs to yuan through Alipay, WeChat Pay and Chinese bank accounts.
In PAPSS's June 2026 mapping Cameroon appeared only in the extended network, receiving funds through one unidentified bank and one mobile wallet, per Africtelegraph.
BEAC joined PAPSS, announced by Afreximbank on 9 July 2026, and CEMAC banks are to be connected to it by end-2026.

TechAfrica News reports on 9 July 2026 that BEAC, serving Cameroon among six CEMAC states, has joined PAPSS, which connects 28 countries and 16 switches, with operationalisation and onboarding of CEMAC institutions planned through end 2026.
PAPSS lists Cameroon as reachable for inbound payments only through its Extended Network partners: one bank and one mobile wallet; no direct participant.
Cameroon is one of six CEMAC states on GIMACPAY, the regional platform whose interoperable QR Code standard was launched on 29 July 2026.
Cameroon takes part in GIMACPAY, the CEMAC regional payment platform operated by GIMAC.
GIMAC reported that the regional GIMACPAY platform processed 20.3 million transactions worth FCFA 863 billion in 2025, up 40% by volume, across the six CEMAC states.
GIMAC statistics presented on 30 July 2026 rank Cameroonian issuers and acquirers (Afriland First Bank, MTN, Orange) in the CEMAC interoperable card and mobile payments network in H1 2026.
Cameroon's Treasury and operators take part in Gimacpay, the Gimac platform serving the Cemac zone, which BEAC data show handling 601.7 billion FCFA by end-2023.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY, live since July 2020, carries domestic and cross-border payments within the six CEMAC states including Cameroon.
AfricaNenda says Cameroon is one of the six CEMAC states served by GIMACPAY, a regional interoperability platform in service.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY processed about 10 million transactions worth $657 million in 2022 across all six states, domestic and cross-border combined.

BEAC launched on 29 July 2026 an interoperable QR code letting any bank or microfinance app in the CEMAC read a merchant code in any member country, with regional operations routed and cleared via GIMAC.

Business in Cameroon reports that Nigerian fintech Grey, in a 7 September 2026 update, opened a corridor sending CFA francs from dollar, euro or pound balances directly to MTN Mobile Money and Orange Money wallets in Cameroon, at $1.80 a transfer and up to CFA400,000.
